What’s new · 1.1

Nook 1.1

DJ, founderNovember 14, 20262 min read

Tables

Some things on a board are comparisons: three apartments by rent and commute, a trip by day and city. Copy the cells from Numbers, Excel or Google Sheets and paste them on a board. They arrive as a table, in a card just wide enough for it. Double-click it to change a cell in a plain grid, where Tab moves along and Return adds a row.

The table is plain Markdown inside the card, so the file still opens in any text editor. There are no formulas, on purpose.

One click selects, a double-click opens

Link cards used to open the moment you clicked them, which made them awkward to move. Now they work like files in Finder: click to select, drag to move, double-click to open. To edit a link’s note, click the note of the selected card.

Center Content

After a long scroll it’s easy to lose your cards. Press ⇧⌘0 and they come back to the middle of the window, at the zoom you were using. With a card selected, that card comes to the middle instead.

Also in 1.1

  • Text is larger at every size, there’s a new Extra Large, and region and column names grow with it.
  • YouTube videos open in your browser.
  • Place cards show the whole map, with the name and the area under it.
  • ⌘Z undoes a delete again.
  • Pasting an image’s address makes an image card.

Nook updates by replacing the app: your boards stay where they are. Full release notes.
